title: DeskClaim
description: How the backend adapter claims a desk on the Enclave before a change, and releases it after. JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Enclave's narrow backend-link socket in the shared socket folder, which carries exactly these three methods and nothing else. A claim takes the SAME lock a job's admission takes, created new, so a governed change and a job never run on one desk at once: the loser is refused DESK_BUSY naming the winner. Only the holder releases. A change that is `ready` or `refused` frees the desk; `unknown` keeps it held, marked, across restarts, until the adapter reconciles it or an operator releases it after reading the desk. Each call is one request object; a refusal is a JSON-RPC error whose message starts with one of `refusal_code` and a colon. Unknown fields are refused.

desk.description: The desk's name, the same rule as the adapter contract's routes.

provider.description: A provider's name, the same rule as the adapter contract's names.

operation_id.description: The change's operation: a lowercase hyphenated UUID, the backend's request id.

outcome.description: How the change ended, in the adapter contract's words. `running` is never released: the claim stays until the change settles.

holder.description: The lock's content when a change holds the desk: `admin:<operation id>`, with ` unknown` appended while its outcome is unknown. A job's lock holds its attempt id instead.

params.description: A read-back saying the desk is gone is sent only with `ready`: a delete whose outcome is unknown has not been read back.

read_back.description: What the adapter read back after a `ready` change, in one of two shapes: the live desk (`read_back_live`), or that the desk is gone (`read_back_deleted`).

read_back_live.description: What the adapter's `status` read back after a `ready` change that moved the desk's accepted configuration. The Enclave files a re-pin to it, and its pin pass pins only if the live desk is exactly this.

read_back_deleted.description: What the adapter read back after a `ready` delete: the backend answered NOT_FOUND for the desk's sandbox id. It frees the lock and retires the desk's pins. `sandbox_id` must equal the sandbox id the Enclave pinned for this desk; any other is refused READ_BACK_MISMATCH and the claim is kept.

claim_result.description: The claim was taken. `required_providers` is what the desk's own record on the Enclave says the desk's agent needs (`desk.agent.providers`), read under the claim, so it cannot change while the claim is held: the adapter refuses DESK_PROVIDER_REQUIRED for a detach of any provider listed here, before any call to the gateway. Empty for a desk the Enclave has no record of, or a new one. Never taken from a label or a request body.

released.description: `freed`: the desk is free. `freed_repin_filed`: free, and a re-pin to the read-back is filed. `freed_pins_retired`: free, and the desk's pins are retired after a read-back saying it is gone. `kept_unknown`: the outcome is unknown and the desk stays held.

holder_id.description: A job's attempt id, or a change's operation id.

locks_result.description: Every desk lock: who holds it, never what it was asked to do.

refusal_code.description: DESK_BUSY: the desk is held by a job (naming its attempt) or another change. DESK_NAME_INVALID, OPERATION_ID_INVALID: a malformed call. DESK_NOT_HELD: no change holds the desk. DESK_HELD_BY_ANOTHER: another change holds it. OUTCOME_INVALID: not one of `outcome`. DESK_CLAIMS_UNAVAILABLE: this Enclave runs no desk executor. READ_BACK_REQUIRED: `ready` for a desk the Enclave has pinned, with no `read_back`; the claim is kept. READ_BACK_MISMATCH: a read-back saying the desk is gone names a sandbox id other than the pinned one; the claim is kept.

code.description: -32602: the params are malformed or carry an unknown field. -32000: refused; the message names why.

message.description: For -32000, one of `refusal_code`, a colon and our own sentence. Never a request body.
